intro: Four outbound campaigns in the UAE: Indian manufacturers building a distributor shortlist, and UAE brokers and IT providers booking meetings with local decision-makers. Every number below comes from a real campaign.

audiences.title: Companies entering the UAE
audiences.body: Indian manufacturers and pharma companies that need an importer or distributor with the right customer coverage, rather than selling to end buyers one by one.

audiences.title: Firms already based in the UAE
audiences.body: Brokers, IT providers and service firms that need earlier meetings with HR, finance and operations heads at UAE companies.

plays.title: Shortlist distributors instead of blasting them
plays.body: An Indian formulation company approached UAE distributors and importers about portfolio fit. Follow-ups asked about customer segments, existing product lines and support for market entry, so only real fits reached a meeting.

plays.title: Reach employers before renewal, not during it
plays.body: A UAE brokerage kept arriving after benefits renewals were decided. Outreach to HR directors, finance heads and owners at employers with 50 to 500 staff established renewal timing first.

plays.title: Qualify partners on after-sales, not just interest
plays.body: An Indian commercial kitchen equipment maker had enquiries from distributors with uneven coverage. Follow-ups checked customer segments, installation support and after-sales capability before any shortlist.

rulesBody: The UAE has a federal Personal Data Protection Law, and free zones such as DIFC and ADGM run their own data protection rules. We contact business decision-makers only, say clearly who is writing and why, and stop at the first opt-out. Check specifics with counsel before scaling.
timingBody: UAE time is 1.5 hours behind India. Messages go out on weekday mornings UAE time, and we avoid Friday afternoons, when many companies keep shorter hours.
